entries.title: A4988 Stepper Motor Driver Carrier, item 1182, PCB md09b

implements.text: Nothing runs in the Studio yet. The page lists the limits of the board and how VREF sets the current limit, for reading.

unsupported.text: The step translator, the microstep tables and the current DAC.
The current limit set by VREF, and the 70.71 percent of it that full step puts in each coil.
The chopper, decay modes and the motor current waveform.
Thermal shutdown at 165 degC, undervoltage lockout, and damage from a reversed or too high supply.

knownFailureCases: The VREF to current-limit rule, the coil path resistance and the shutdown temperature are constants in the figure page, not in the Studio solver.
No test checks the current limit against the datasheet.

entries.title: 4 x AA battery holder

implements.text: Nothing runs. The drawing shows the pack and a bench model's reported voltage and state.

unsupported.text: Supply voltage, sag under load, internal resistance, reverse connection and discharge. The Studio does not run it until the solver has a voltage source element.

knownFailureCases: No voltage source element exists in the solver (the figure has no elec line), so the layer is none.
The figure's 1.6 V fresh cell and 0.15 to 0.3 ohm internal resistance are quoted from Energizer E91 data in a comment. That data sheet was not read here, and no value is stored.

implements.text: The I2C slave answers at its address and returns raw temperature, pressure and humidity words that the Bosch integer compensation turns back into the inputs.
Conversion time, forced and normal mode, standby time, soft reset, and CTRL_HUM taking effect at the next CTRL_MEAS write.

unsupported.text: SPI mode (CSB low), the IIR filter, self-heating, sleep current, and sensor thermal lag.
Damage above the 4.25 V maximum.
A BMP280 look-alike board that reads chip ID 0x58 and has no humidity.
The calibration words are a synthetic set, not a dump from a physical chip.

entries.title: Half-size breadboard

implements.text: Each column half of five holes and each power rail is one conductor.

unsupported.text: Contact resistance, stray capacitance between strips and the break in the middle of a long power rail.

knownFailureCases: The rails are continuous here. Some half-size boards split them; this one is modelled as unbroken.

entries.title: 12 mm piezo buzzer, passive or active

implements.text: A load across the two pins, and the tone() frequency of the pin it hangs on, reported as sound.
A steady HIGH makes a click on the passive kind and the fixed tone on the active kind.

unsupported.text: Sound output, loudness against frequency beyond the resonance curve in the figure, and the buzzer's own current draw over time.
The magnetic 16 ohm kind, which needs a transistor on a board.

knownFailureCases: The test covers the passive kind only.

entries.title: 130-size brushed DC motor, 3 to 6 V

implements.text: A two-lead brushed motor that draws the no-load current plus the propeller current once it spins, starts above one volt average and stops below 0.6 V.
Stall current of the supply voltage over the armature resistance when the shaft is held.
A winding that burns out above 9 V and a switch-off spike when there is no flyback diode.

unsupported.text: Motor speed against torque beyond the propeller case, and the shaft inertia.
Brush noise and the heat of the winding over time.

knownFailureCases: Every number is a constant in the figure with no source. The fact sheet gives FA-130RA values and marks them unverified, so all of them sit in the simulation slot with low confidence.
The solver stamps the motor between two nodes and reads only the resistance and a current table, not the back-EMF constant.
The load option (prop, free, stalled) changes the figure and the old solver loop but is not wired to a model parameter here; the propeller current is always used.
No test checks a number. Motors, servos and steppers have no golden-trace shape, so the one fixture only checks that the layers resolve and every pin and rating is wired.

entries.title: 1N4007 rectifier diode

implements.text: Conduction above a fixed 0.7 V with a 0.2 ohm slope.
Blocking in reverse.
Burn-out above 1 A average or 30 A peak.

unsupported.text: The exponential forward curve: the figure's fit gives 0.56 V at 1 mA and 0.91 V at 1 A, the solver gives 0.7 V throughout.
Reverse breakdown and the 1000 V rating.
Reverse recovery, leakage and temperature.

knownFailureCases: The solver uses a fixed 0.7 V and 0.2 ohm for every diode. The figure states 0.8 V, n 1.808, rs 34 milliohm and a SPICE fit, none of which the solver reads.
The figure's type selector (1N4001 to 1N4007) is not carried. This part is the 1N4007; the other types have no descriptor.
The burn-out rule has a 30 A peak condition besides the 1 A average. Only the average is written as a failure mode.

entries.title: 4010 axial fan, 5 V, brushless

implements.text: A brushless fan as a motor element that stalls below 2.5 V average and runs above it.
A driver chip that fails above 6.5 V.
A switch-off spike when no flyback diode is across the fan.

unsupported.text: Speed as a function of voltage inside the solver: the figure draws it, the element reads no speed.
Airflow, noise and the Hall sensor.

knownFailureCases: Every number is a figure constant with no source. The ratings the figure cites came from distributor listings that nobody read for this file, so all sit in the simulation slot.
The figure sets polar: true and draws a fan that does not spin when reversed, but the motor element has no polarity rule, so this part lists no reverse-polarity failure mode.
No test checks a number. Motors, servos and steppers have no golden-trace shape, so the one fixture only checks that the layers resolve and every pin and rating is wired.

entries.title: Force-sensing resistor, FSR 402

implements.text: The unloaded sensor as a 10 megohm resistor.

unsupported.text: Resistance that follows force.
Hysteresis, drift under load and part-to-part spread.
Force below the 0.2 N threshold acting as a true open circuit; the model keeps a 10 megohm path.

operatingRange.evidence: Newtons. Only the unloaded case is modelled.

knownFailureCases: The resistance does not follow force until a curve model kind exists (Q1). The figure interpolates log R against log F in fsr402.js:19 and passes the result to the solver.
The figure removes the element below the threshold (open: true). The descriptor keeps a 10 megohm resistor instead.

entries.title: GY-521 breakout with MPU-6050

implements.text: The I2C slave at 0x68 or 0x69 with the sample, range, sleep, reset and WHO_AM_I registers.
Power-on in sleep: samples read 0 until the host clears the sleep bit.
Sensitivity per range for the accelerometer, gyroscope and temperature, with 16-bit signed output and clamping.
A constant gyro bias, so integrating the rate drifts.
The board's over-voltage and reversed-supply failures.

unsupported.text: Noise, temperature drift and part-to-part spread: the datasheet gives them and the model does not apply them.
The digital low-pass filter, sample-rate divider, FIFO, interrupts and the DMP.
The auxiliary I2C master and any magnetometer behind it.
I2C timing: clock speed, clock stretching and start-up delay.
Pull-up variants of 2.2k or 10k, and the second regulator type (A249).
Damage from 5 V on the logic pins.
The 3.3 V regulator and the power LED: both are rules in the figure page, not in the solver.
In the Studio's register map only ACCEL_ZOUT, PWR_MGMT_1 and WHO_AM_I exist. The gyroscope, temperature, X and Y registers and the range selects are in the sketch interpreter's class only.

parameterSources.ref: ps_mpu Absolute maximum ratings: VDD + 0.5 V
umw_digikey Product attributes: output voltage 3.3 V
ps_mpu Electrical characteristics: gyro and accelerometer on, DMP off
ps_mpu Serial interface: I2C fast mode
ps_mpu Electrical characteristics: start-up time for register read and write
ps_mpu Gyroscope specifications: ZRO initial tolerance, 25 C
ps_mpu Gyroscope specifications: total RMS noise, DLPF_CFG = 2
ps_mpu Accelerometer specifications: zero-g initial calibration tolerance, X and Y

knownFailureCases: The module figure prints its own sample text from a second, simpler model, not from this register model.
One test reads 1 g on Z after waking the chip; no test checks the sensitivities or the reset values against the datasheet.
Two models of the chip exist: the Studio's register map and the sketch interpreter's class. They agree on WHO_AM_I, the sleep bit and the Z reading but not on the rest.

entries.title: HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranging module

implements.text: Nothing in the Studio yet. The sketch interpreter runs class HcSr04: a 10 microsecond trigger starts a ping and Echo is HIGH for 58.3 microseconds per centimetre.

unsupported.text: The transmit driver, the receive amplifier and the comparator: the board is treated as two pins.
Soft and angled targets, the 15 degree beam and the speed of sound changing with temperature.
A clone whose Echo stays HIGH after a missed ping, and the HC-SR04P 3.3 V variant.
Damage from reversed or too high a supply.

knownFailureCases: The card for this part expected a registered device, but only the register-map devices mpu6050, bme280, ssd1306 and pca9685 are registered. HcSr04 is a class the interpreter picks by name.
No test checks the echo width against the 58 microseconds per centimetre rule.

entries.title: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver module (red, 43 x 43 mm)

implements.text: Nothing runs in the Studio yet. The page lists the limits of the board, its seven faults and the truth table of one channel for reading.

mocked.text: The overtemperature cut-out is a timer: with the stall fault set, the outputs switch off for 2 s of every 5 s once 6 s have passed.
Overtemperature cut-out on a stalled motor

unsupported.text: The two H-bridges: drive, brake and coast, with the enable as a duty from 0 to 1.
The voltage lost in the switches, which the figure fits to the datasheet typical totals at 1 A and 2 A.
The 5V-EN regulator, and the over-voltage and under-voltage thresholds the board is known to have.
Heat in the chip and the overtemperature cut-out.
Motor back-EMF, inductance and the flyback current through the eight diodes.
Switching loss, PWM frequency limits, ripple, damage above 2 A and any current limit.
The analog level on the inputs, clone chips and part-to-part variation.

parameterSources.ref: facts Recommended operating conditions, VS: VIH + 2.5 V to 46 V
facts Features: input voltage (LM78M05 product page, via the fact sheet)
facts Electrical characteristics, input low voltage
facts Electrical characteristics, input high voltage
facts Absolute maximum ratings, Vi and Ven
facts Absolute maximum ratings, DC output current per channel
facts VCEsat(H) + VCEsat(L) at IL = 1 A
facts VCEsat(H) + VCEsat(L) at IL = 2 A
facts Electrical characteristics, IS with enable high and input high
facts Thermal data, operating junction temperature -25 to 130 degC

operatingRange.evidence: The range of the datasheet curve the drop fit follows.

knownFailureCases: The bridge assumes a fixed 0.6 A motor and a 3 ohm stall resistance instead of reading the motor that is attached.
The overtemperature cut-out switches the outputs off for 2 s of every 5 s once 6 s have passed with the stall fault set. It does not read the computed junction temperature.
No test checks the drop fit or the truth table against the datasheet; the existing tests check texts and ids only.

entries.title: Light-dependent resistor GL5528

implements.text: A fixed resistor of about 1.9 kilohm, the value at 300 lux.

unsupported.text: Resistance that follows the light level.
The 20 ms and 30 ms response lag.
Power and voltage limits: the solver never overheats a resistor.
Temperature and part-to-part spread.

operatingRange.evidence: The model is a fixed value at the default light level only.

knownFailureCases: The resistance does not follow light until a curve model kind exists (Q1). The figure computes ohmsAt(lux) in ldr.js:16 and the solver is given that value per run.
The figure passes lag [0.02, 0.03] to the solver, which does not read it.

entries.title: 5 mm through-hole LED

implements.text: Forward conduction as a fixed forward voltage per colour plus a 0.5 ohm slope.
Burn-out above 2.5 times the continuous current rating.
A backwards LED passes no current and is flagged.
Relative brightness from current, for the drawing only.

unsupported.text: The exponential diode curve: below about 1 mA the model is off or on, not gradual.
Reverse breakdown and the reverse voltage rating.
Temperature, ageing and part-to-part spread in forward voltage.
Pulsed or PWM peak ratings: the burn rule uses one factor for any pulse.
Light output as a physical unit.

operatingRange.evidence: The range of the RS-08 comparison cases C06 to C10.

knownFailureCases: At 0.3 mA the solver reads 0.299 mA where a realistic LED model reads 0.321 mA (7 percent).
The green option is a GaP green. A pure green LED needs a 3.0 V forward voltage that this part does not offer.

entries.title: 2S LiPo battery (7.4 V)

implements.text: Nothing runs. The drawing shows the pack and a bench model's reported voltage and state.

unsupported.text: Supply voltage, sag under load, internal resistance, reverse connection and discharge. The Studio does not run it until the solver has a voltage source element.

knownFailureCases: No voltage source element exists in the solver (the figure has no elec line), so the layer is none.
The mechanics battery block is left out. It needs a cell resistance, and the figure states none.
The 8.4 V full, 7.4 V nominal and 1000 mAh figures are the figure's own text. No datasheet was read.

entries.title: LM2596 DC-DC step-down module with LED voltmeter (2596-SDC)

implements.text: Nothing is solved here. The module page computes the output voltage, efficiency, current limit and heat for its own display.

unsupported.text: The output voltage from the trimmer setting and the input.
Losses in the switch, the catch diode and the inductor, and the heat they make.
The 4.5 A peak current limit and the thermal shutdown.
Damage from a reversed or over-voltage input: the board has no protection.
The 3-digit voltmeter and its IN and OUT select button.

knownFailureCases: The whole converter model, built from the datasheet curves in the fact sheet, is code in the module page and is not data.
No test checks the converter against the datasheet curves.

entries.title: Pocket digital multimeter

implements.text: Nothing yet: the part places two probe tips and a drawing of the meter.

unsupported.text: The reading, the range dial and the loading of the circuit by the meter.
The current ranges and the 10 A jack.

knownFailureCases: The displayed reading is computed by the bench that uses the meter, not by this descriptor.

entries.title: NEMA 17 stepper motor (SY42STH38-1684A class)

implements.text: Nothing runs. The part page and the bench drawing show the shaft angle and coil currents that a driver module reports.

unsupported.text: Coil current, step loss, pull-out torque and heating. The motor numbers are stored for the robot engine and no layer reads them yet.
The Studio does not run it until a bipolar stepper element exists in the solver.

knownFailureCases: No bipolar stepper element exists in the solver, so the layer is none.
The motor numbers come from a fact sheet that quotes the SOYO datasheet. This descriptor did not read the datasheet.
No pull-out torque curve is stored, because none is stated in the figure or the fact sheet.

entries.title: 2N2222A NPN transistor, TO-92

implements.text: A saturating switch: a fixed base-emitter drop, a fixed gain and a fixed saturation voltage.
A transistor fitted backwards, with a gain of 5 from collector to emitter.
Failure by heat or by a collector peak above 1.5 times the current rating.
A hot state above 0.75 times the power rating.

unsupported.text: The change of gain, base-emitter drop and saturation voltage with current.
The linear region, switching speed and capacitance.
Temperature effects on gain and the base-emitter drop.
The collector-emitter and emitter-base voltage ratings.

operatingRange.evidence: Up to the continuous rating in the figure header.

knownFailureCases: The figure lets you pick the pin order EBC or CBE. A descriptor cannot swap terminals by a parameter, so this one fixes EBC and the C B E order of P2N2222A parts is not represented.
The solver uses 0.7 V and 0.2 V at any current, while the figure's own curves move between 0.6 and 1.2 V and between 0.05 and 0.3 V.

entries.title: 16-Channel 12-bit PWM/Servo Driver, product 815, rev C

implements.text: An I2C slave at 0x40 with the register map the libraries use: MODE1 with its sleep and auto-increment bits, PRE_SCALE and sixteen on and off counts.
PRE_SCALE is ignored unless MODE1 SLEEP is set, and the chip powers up asleep at 200 Hz with every output off.
The duty and pulse width of each channel, worked out from the counts and the 25 MHz oscillator, with the full-on and full-off bits.

unsupported.text: The oscillator error: the clock is a fixed 25 MHz, where a board runs between 23 and 27 MHz.
The All Call address 0x70 and the software reset call.
The OE pin, MODE2 and the output drive mode, and the voltage on the outputs.
The servo supply, the reverse-polarity MOSFET, the power LED and the jumpers on the address pins.

knownFailureCases: The model's oscillator is 25 MHz with no error, so a program that calibrates it sees no effect.
There is no numeric test of the pulse width or the frequency; only the conformance checks run.

entries.title: B10K rotary potentiometer, 9 mm

implements.text: A linear taper: the wiper divides the track in proportion to the knob position.
A track that gets hot or burns when too much power goes through a short stretch of it.

unsupported.text: Wiper contact resistance and noise.
Log taper and tolerance: the end-to-end value is the stated value.
The 300 degree sweep: the position is a number from 0 to 1.

knownFailureCases: At either end the solver keeps 0.5 ohm between the wiper and the end, so a pot turned fully over is never a perfect short.

entries.title: 6 x 6 mm tactile push button, 4 legs

implements.text: Two always-joined pairs of legs, and a press that joins the pairs.
A button whose switched legs sit in one breadboard strip counts as shorted.

unsupported.text: Contact bounce, contact resistance and the 50 mA and 24 V contact ratings: the numbers are stored but no check reads them.
Operating force and travel.

knownFailureCases: imax, vmax and bounce are passed to the solver, which does not read them yet.

entries.title: QTR-8RC reflectance sensor array

implements.text: Nothing in the Studio yet. The figure page computes each sensor's fall time from the line position, the supply and the faults in force.

unsupported.text: The phototransistor, the infrared LEDs and the RC nodes as circuit elements.
Height above the floor, surface colour and the light that comes back: the figure takes them from a mode.
The 2-sensor piece that snaps off, and the 3.3V BYPASS pads as a build option.
Damage from reversed or too high a supply.

knownFailureCases: The solver has no element that turns a light level into a pin fall time, so no layer can run.
The white decay and the 1.6 power in the light response are fitted in the figure, with no source.

entries.title: Resistor, through-hole

implements.text: Ideal linear resistance between two pins.

unsupported.text: Tolerance, temperature coefficient, power rating and burn-out.
Lead inductance and parasitic capacitance.

knownFailureCases: A resistor never overheats in the model, whatever the current.
No test checks a resistor divider on its own; the series case above is the only one.

entries.title: RGB LED, 5 mm, common cathode

implements.text: Three diodes sharing a cathode, one forward voltage per colour plus a 0.5 ohm slope.
Burn-out of one colour above 2.5 times its continuous current rating.

unsupported.text: Common-anode wiring.
Brightness and the mixed colour; the drawing works them out from the solved currents.
Temperature and part-to-part spread in forward voltage.

operatingRange.evidence: The range the single LED was compared over; the RGB part has no comparison of its own.

knownFailureCases: Common anode is not represented. The common parameter has no effect on the model, which is always common cathode.
No numeric test exists: the golden harness has no shape for three diodes with a shared lead.
The descriptor has no brightness layer; the figure computes brightness from current in rgb-led.js:46.

entries.title: TowerPro SG90 micro servo

implements.text: A three-lead servo that loads its supply through V+ and GND with a small constant conductance.

unsupported.text: The pulse on SIG: arm angle, dead band and the end stop are drawn by the figure only.
Moving and stall current: the element stamps a fixed load, so the 200 mA and 700 mA figures are shown but not drawn.
Gear wear and the potentiometer on the output shaft.

knownFailureCases: The idle, moving and stall currents are seller figures from the fact sheet, marked unverified there. They sit in the simulation slot, not as datasheet values.
The solver servo element reads no signal; pulse width to angle is figure code only. The servo-pwm protocol is listed as not modelled yet.
No test checks a number. Motors, servos and steppers have no golden-trace shape, so the one fixture only checks that the layers resolve and every pin and rating is wired.

entries.title: Capacitive soil moisture sensor v1.2

implements.text: Nothing is solved. The figure draws the probe, the pot and the cable, and the moisture setting darkens the soil.

unsupported.text: The 555 oscillator, the pad as one plate of a capacitor, the peak detector and the bleed resistor.
The AOUT level that falls as the soil gets wetter.
The NE555 clone that never starts on 3.3 V, and the clone without a bleed resistor.

knownFailureCases: The AOUT level, the NE555 and bleed-resistor variants and the watering cycle live in the module page only.
No test checks the AOUT level against a measurement. The 2.6 V and 1.4 V ends are the figure's constants, not maker figures.

entries.title: 0.96 inch 128 x 64 I2C OLED module with SSD1306

implements.text: ACK at the set address.
Display on and off, invert and contrast commands.
A 1-bit framebuffer written by the library and drawn on the module.

unsupported.text: Scrolling, addressing modes, charge pump and panel voltage.
Bus timing and clock stretching.
Supply range: the 3.3 to 5 V window is shown but no model reads it.

entries.title: 28BYJ-48 geared stepper, 5 V

implements.text: Four coils of 50 ohm from the common red lead to the blue, pink, yellow and orange leads.

unsupported.text: Which coils are energised and in what order: step sequences, speed and stall stay in the figure.
Coil inductance, the gearbox and the torque.

knownFailureCases: Full, half and wave step tables, the pin-order check and the stall rate are figure code. The descriptor holds the coil resistance only.
The fact sheet gives pull-in and self-positioning torque but no holding torque, so the mechanics block is left out.
The coil resistance and the 5 V rating come from the fact sheet's quote of the datasheet, which was not read here, so they sit in the simulation slot.
No test checks a number. Motors, servos and steppers have no golden-trace shape, so the one fixture only checks that the layers resolve and every pin and rating is wired.

entries.title: Motor Driver - Dual TB6612FNG (1A), ROB-14451, board v1.1c

implements.text: Nothing runs in the Studio yet. The page lists the limits of the board and the truth table of one channel for reading.

unsupported.text: The two H-bridges: drive, reverse, short brake, stop and standby.
The voltage lost in the bridge, about 0.5 ohm, which the figure applies to a fixed running current.
Thermal shutdown at 175 degC, and the 1 A operating limit.
Damage from a reversed or too high supply.

knownFailureCases: The bridge truth table and the 0.5 ohm drop live in the figure page and are not available to the Studio solver.
The figure assumes a motor running current of 0.15 A instead of reading the attached motor.
No test checks the bridge against the datasheet.

entries.title: TIP120 NPN Darlington transistor, TO-220

implements.text: A saturating Darlington switch with the stated minimum gain of 1000, a 1.3 V base drop and a 0.9 V saturation drop.
A transistor fitted backwards, with a gain of 5 from collector to emitter.
Failure by heat or by a collector peak above 1.5 times the current rating, with a burnt part shorting collector to emitter.
A hot state above 0.75 times the free-air power rating, and an overdriven state above the base current rating.

unsupported.text: The two internal transistors and the 8 kilohm and 120 ohm resistors: the model sees one transistor.
The change of base drop and saturation drop with current.
The built-in diode some makers show from emitter to collector.
A heatsink: the power rating is the free-air one.

parameterSources.ref: factsheet hFE >= 1000 at VCE 3 V, IC 0.5 A and 3 A

operatingRange.evidence: The lesson currents the base and saturation drops were read for.

knownFailureCases: The solver uses 1.3 V and 0.9 V at any current. At 3 A the sheet allows up to 2.5 V and 2.0 V.
The 62.5 degC per watt is worked back from the 2 W free-air rating, not stated by the maker.

entries.title: TMP36 temperature sensor

implements.text: A powered output at one held voltage, 0.72 V, with 20 ohms of output resistance.
No output below 2.7 V or above 7 V on the supply.
Burn-out from a reversed or too high supply.

unsupported.text: Output that follows temperature in the descriptor layer; the live adapter sets it from the temperature setting.
Accuracy of +-2 degrees C and self-heating.
Supply current that changes with temperature.

knownFailureCases: The layer holds the output at the default temperature. The live circuit builder sets it from the temperature setting in live.ts.
No numeric test exists: the golden harness has no shape for a powered sensor.
The quiescent current is shown but the solver draws a fixed small conductance.

entries.title: Traffic-light LED module

implements.text: Nothing is solved. The figure lights each lamp from the pin its leg is wired to while the sketch runs.

unsupported.text: The current in each lamp: the resistor, the forward voltage and the pin driver.
A lamp burning out when its resistor is removed.
The 3.3 V board case, where each lamp takes 3 to 4 mA.

knownFailureCases: The lamp current, the 330 ohm resistor and the forward voltages of 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 V live in the module page only.
The part figure draws a 14 x 30 mm board and the module page a 56 x 21 mm one. The dimensions here follow the part figure.

entries.title: TT gear motor, 3 to 6 V, 1:48

unsupported.text: Everything. The figure has no elec line, so the solver sees a TT motor as nothing. The robotics benches model it in their own figure code until B13.

knownFailureCases: tt-motor.js has no elec line, so there is no legacy model to port.
The figure uses a 4 ohm armature and a back-EMF constant for its own drawing; they are not given here because they have no source.

entries.title: ULN2003 stepper driver board for the 28BYJ-48 (35 x 32 mm)

implements.text: Four channels, each a 2.7 kohm base resistor, a Darlington transistor and a clamp diode to the + rail, built from the solver's resistor, transistor and diode elements.
A high input pulls its output down to about 1 V above ground, so a coil from + to that output carries current.

unsupported.text: The four LEDs and their 1 kohm resistors.
The power-on jumper: the model assumes the cap is fitted.
The motor itself and the step sequence; both belong to the stepper part and the program.
Heat in the chip, and damage above 0.5 A a channel or 50 V.

knownFailureCases: The transistor gain and base-emitter drop come from constants in the part figure, and the diode drop from the solver's fixed value. None has a datasheet source.
There is no numeric test of the saturation voltage against the datasheet; only the conformance checks run.

entries.title: Arduino UNO Rev3

implements.text: Arduino-C++ subset run by the interpreter with the Uno pin map.
Digital I/O on D0 to D13 and A0 to A5, PWM on D3, D5, D6, D9, D10 and D11, interrupts on D2 and D3.
10-bit analog reads against a 5 V reference, I2C master on SDA and SCL, serial output, and the L LED on D13.

unsupported.text: The AVR core, timers, bootloader and flash behaviour.
The 5 V and 3.3 V regulators, the USB power switch and the brown-out level.
Pin current limits and the ICSP headers.

knownFailureCases: No electrical ratings are listed yet, so no pin-overload check exists for this board.
